title: Phase 0: Safety & Correctness
description: P0 priority — Fix critical safety bugs before any feature work. Includes: (1) Replace pkill -f with Treehouse.return() for workspace cleanup, (2) Add crash cleanup lifecycle with PeerCrashed event, (3) Add VerifyProfile-based verification before accept. All existing tests must pass. New safety tests required.

title: 0.1: Replace pkill -f with Treehouse.return()
description:
BUG (P0): pkill -f regex at crates/anti-daemon/src/main.rs:629 can match and kill current Claude session. The pattern `claude -p.*{worktree_path}` uses regex on full command line — blast radius is dangerous.

FIX: Replace pkill -f with Treehouse.return_if_lease(). Boundary contract:
- PeerManager owns PROCESS lifecycle (spawn/wait/terminate by PID)
- TreehouseAdapter owns WORKSPACE lifecycle (lease/worktree/cleanup)
- On peer exit: PeerManager detects → emits PeerCrashed → handler calls TreehouseAdapter.release_if_lease()

Files to modify:
- crates/anti-daemon/src/main.rs:629 — replace pkill block with Treehouse.return_if_lease()
- crates/anti-workspace/src/lib.rs — add return_if_lease() method if not present

Edge cases:
- What if Treehouse binary not found? Fallback to manual worktree cleanup
- What if lease already released? Idempotent — return Ok(())
- What if process still running? PeerManager.terminate() first, then Treehouse.return

Verification:
1. Spawn peer → verify worktree exists in treehouse pool
2. Kill peer process (not via pkill!)
3. Wait for reaper to detect exit
4. Verify worktree cleaned up via Treehouse status
5. Verify current Claude session (this one) is unaffected
6. Run: cargo test --workspace — all existing tests pass

title: 0.2: Crash cleanup lifecycle
description:
CRASH CLEANUP LIFECYCLE (P0): Current reaper (main.rs:202-207) only calls mark_exit() which sets status to CRASHED/COMPLETED but does NOT cleanup workspace or emit structured events.

TARGET: Full crash lifecycle:
1. Reaper detects process exit via try_wait() (main.rs:468)
2. mark_exit() sets status + emits AgentCrashed event (existing)
3. NEW: Check if agent had workspace lease
4. NEW: If lease exists → Treehouse.return_if_lease() (cleanup worktree)
5. NEW: Persist crash evidence (exit_code, signal, timestamp)
6. NEW: Emit PeerCrashed lifecycle event with structured data
7. Lead decides: retry / replace / abort (not auto-retry!)

Files to modify:
- crates/anti-daemon/src/main.rs — enhance reap_children() to call cleanup after mark_exit
- crates/anti-core/src/events.rs — add PeerCrashed event type with exit info

Existing code reference:
- main.rs:468 — reap_children() calls mark_exit(id, ok)
- main.rs:423 — reconcile_on_start() checks PID liveness on daemon restart
- events.rs:20 — AgentCrashed exists but lacks structured crash data

Edge cases:
- Multiple rapid crashes → don't spam cleanup (debounce)
- Workspace already released by sweeper → idempotent
- Treehouse binary missing → log warning, skip cleanup
- Daemon restart while cleanup in progress → SQLite state is source of truth

Tests:
- spawn peer → kill peer → wait for reaper → verify workspace cleaned
- spawn peer → kill peer → verify PeerCrashed event emitted
- daemon restart with dead peer → verify cleanup runs on restart

title: 0.3: VerifyProfile-based verification
description:
VERIFYPROFILE VERIFICATION (P0): Current accept requires Verified state but there's no automated verification — it's manual via CLI. Need programmatic verification with evidence.

ARCHITECTURE:
- VerifyProfile enum defines WHAT checks to run (not arbitrary commands)
- Verifier executes the profile and captures evidence
- VerificationResult stores all evidence for audit trail
- State machine: Submitted → Verified (only via verify command)

VerifyProfile variants:
- Full: cargo fmt --check + cargo clippy + cargo test + cargo build
- Check: cargo fmt --check + cargo clippy + cargo test (no build)
- Test: cargo test only
- Build: cargo build only
- Named(String): loaded from .anti_subagent/verify.toml config

Why profiles, not commands:
- Prevents execution escape hatch (caller can't inject arbitrary CLI)
- Evidence is comparable across runs (same profile = same checks)
- Configurable per-project but not per-call

VerificationResult struct:
- status: VerifyStatus (Pass | Fail | Incomplete)
- profile: VerifyProfile (which profile was used)
- test_output: Option<String> (stdout+stderr from cargo test)
- build_output: Option<String> (stdout+stderr from cargo build)
- diagnostics: Vec<String> (clippy warnings, type errors)
- git_diff: Option<String> (changes since last verify)
- git_sha: Option<String> (commit at verify time)
- claims_verified: Vec<ClaimVerification> (acceptance criteria)
- timestamp: String (when verification ran)

Files to modify:
- crates/anti-core/src/work.rs — add VerifyProfile, VerificationResult structs
- crates/anti-daemon/src/ipc.rs — add VerifyWork request variant
- crates/anti-daemon/src/main.rs — add verify handler (spawn cargo subprocess)
- crates/anti-cli/src/main.rs — add verify subcommand with --profile flag
- crates/anti-cli/src/commands.rs — add verify handler

Integration with existing state machine:
- work.rs already has can_transition(Submitted, Verified)
- Verify handler: run profile → if all pass → transition to Verified
- If any fail → stay at Submitted, return VerificationResult with failures

Tests:
- verify with Full profile on passing code → Verified + evidence
- verify with Test profile on failing tests → Submitted + failure evidence
- verify with nonexistent config → error message
- accept without verify → still blocked (existing test)

title: Phase 1: Execution Architecture
description: P1 — 2 weeks. Staged task state machine (RECEIVED→EXPLORED→PLANNED→EXECUTING→VERIFYING→ACCEPTED), EvidenceRecord model (git diff, test output, build output, diagnostics), Writer-Verifier separation via disposition contracts. Depends on Phase 0 safety fixes.

title: 1.1: Staged task state machine
description:
STAGED TASK STATE MACHINE (P1): Current WorkItemState has 7 states (Pending/InProgress/Submitted/Verified/Accepted/NeedsRevision/Rejected). Need to expand to support full lifecycle.

NEW STATES (12 total):
- RECEIVED: task assigned to peer
- EXPLORED: peer has investigated codebase
- PLANNED: implementation plan created
- EXECUTING: peer actively coding
- EXECUTED: code written, awaiting verification
- VERIFYING: verification in progress
- VERIFIED: verification passed (prerequisite for accept)
- ACCEPTED: lead accepted (terminal)
- FAILED: execution failed (terminal)
- REJECTED: verification failed, needs fix
- FIXING: peer fixing issues
- EXHAUSTED: max_revisions exceeded (terminal)

TRANSITION TABLE (can_transition):
- Pending → InProgress (existing)
- InProgress → Submitted (existing)
- Submitted → Verified (via verify command)
- Submitted → NeedsRevision (via reject)
- Verified → Accepted (via accept)
- Verified → NeedsRevision (via reject)
- NeedsRevision → InProgress (via re-submit)
- NEED NEW:
  - Any → Received (task assignment)
  - Received → Explored (investigation done)
  - Explored → Planned (plan created)
  - Planned → Executing (implementation start)
  - Executing → Executed (code complete)
  - Executing → Failed (error)
  - Executed → Verifying (verify started)
  - Verifying → Verified (pass)
  - Verifying → Rejected (fail)
  - Rejected → Fixing (fix started)
  - Fixing → Executing (re-implement)
  - Rejected → Exhausted (max_revisions)

BACKWARD COMPATIBILITY:
- Existing Pending/InProgress/Submitted/Verified/Accepted/NeedsRevision/Rejected states kept
- New states are ADDITIONS, not replacements
- Old CLI commands still work (submit → Submitted, reject → NeedsRevision)
- New staged workflow is opt-in via new IPC commands

Files to modify:
- crates/anti-core/src/work.rs — expand WorkItemState enum + can_transition
- crates/anti-daemon/src/store.rs — migration for new state columns

Tests:
- staged pipeline: Received→Explored→Planned→Executing→Executed→Verifying→Verified→Accepted
- fix loop: Verifying→Rejected→Fixing→Executing→Verifying→Verified→Accepted
- exhaustion: Rejected (rev 3) → Exhausted (terminal)
- backward compat: old Pending→InProgress→Submitted still works

title: 1.2: EvidenceRecord model
description:
EVIDENCE RECORD MODEL (P1): Current EvidenceRef only has sha256 + artifact_path + produced_at. Need comprehensive evidence for audit trail.

CURRENT (work.rs):
- EvidenceRef { sha256, artifact_path, produced_at }
- Used in WorkItem.submit() and WorkItem.reject()

TARGET EvidenceRecord struct:
- Integrity: artifact_sha256, artifact_path
- Test evidence: test_output (Option<String>), test_exit_code (Option<i32>)
- Build evidence: build_output (Option<String>), build_exit_code (Option<i32>)
- Lint evidence: lint_output (Option<String>)
- Diagnostics: diagnostics (Vec<String>) — clippy warnings, type errors
- Git state: git_sha (Option<String>), git_diff (Option<String>), git_status (Option<String>)
- Acceptance criteria: claims (Vec<ClaimVerification>)
- Metadata: produced_at, verified_at (Option<String>), verified_by (Option<String>)

ClaimVerification struct:
- claim: String (what was claimed)
- status: VerifyStatus (Verified | Partial | Missing)
- evidence: Option<String> (supporting data)

DATABASE MIGRATION:
- New table: evidence_records (id, work_item_id, all fields above)
- FK to work_items.id
- Index on work_item_id for fast lookup
- Backward compat: existing EvidenceRef data → migrate to EvidenceRecord with sha256 only

Files to modify:
- crates/anti-core/src/work.rs — add EvidenceRecord, ClaimVerification structs
- crates/anti-daemon/src/store.rs — add evidence_records table + CRUD methods

Integration:
- Verify handler (0.3) creates EvidenceRecord after running profile
- WorkItem stores reference to latest EvidenceRecord
- Accept requires EvidenceRecord with status=Pass

Tests:
- create EvidenceRecord with all fields → serialize/deserialize
- migrate existing EvidenceRef → EvidenceRecord
- query EvidenceRecord by work_item_id

title: 1.3: Disposition contracts (basic)
description:
DISPOSITION CONTRACTS (P1): Current model.rs has Disposition enum with 6 variants (Engineer/Architect/Reviewer/Scout/ProofAuditor/Shadow) but no behavioral contracts.

TARGET: DispositionContract struct defines what each disposition CAN and CANNOT do:
- name: Disposition (existing enum)
- allowed_tools: Vec<String> (tools this disposition may use)
- denied_tools: Vec<String> (tools this disposition may NOT use)
- can_approve_own_work: bool (Engineer=false, ProofAuditor=false)
- requires_evidence: bool (ProofAuditor=true)
- max_concurrent: usize (how many peers with this disposition can run)

CONTRACT TABLE:
| Disposition | CAN | CANNOT | Self-Approve | Evidence Required |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Engineer | read, write, test, edit | approve own work | No | No |
| Architect | read, design, plan | modify implementation | No | No |
| Scout | read, search, inspect | modify source | No | No |
| Reviewer | inspect, test, challenge | silently modify | No | Yes |
| ProofAuditor | read, test, inspect git/logs | modify source | No | Yes |
| Shadow | read, observe | modify anything | No | No |

FILES:
- crates/anti-core/src/disposition.rs (NEW) — DispositionContract + contracts for each disposition
- crates/anti-core/src/model.rs — keep existing Disposition enum, reference from contracts

INTEGRATION:
- PeerManager checks DispositionContract before allowing tool execution
- Guard (ipc.rs GuardCheck) enhanced to use contracts
- Verify handler requires ProofAuditor disposition

Tests:
- Engineer denied self-approval → error
- Scout denied write tool → error
- ProofAuditor requires evidence → error if no EvidenceRecord
- Each disposition's allowed/denied tool lists correct

title: 2.2: Lifecycle event bus
Phase 3: Scheduling & Routing
description: P3 — 2 weeks. Config-based model routing (disposition × complexity → capability tier → provider config), parallel scheduler (resource-aware, dependency-aware). Depends on Phase 2 orchestration.

title: 3.1: Config-based model routing
description:
CONFIG-BASED MODEL ROUTING (P3): Model names should NOT be hard-coded in anti-core. Use provider config for flexibility.

ARCHITECTURE:
- CapabilityTier enum: Lightweight / Standard / Heavyweight
- Route resolution: Disposition x Complexity -> CapabilityTier -> model (from config)
- ProviderConfig loaded from .anti_subagent/providers.toml

CapabilityTier mapping:
- Scout, Shadow -> always Lightweight
- Engineer + Low complexity -> Standard
- Engineer + High complexity -> Heavyweight
- Reviewer, Architect -> Standard
- ProofAuditor -> Heavyweight

Provider config format (.anti_subagent/providers.toml):
  [providers.claude]
  lightweight = haiku
  standard = sonnet
  heavyweight = opus

  [providers.codex]
  lightweight = gpt-4o-mini
  standard = gpt-4o
  heavyweight = o3

Files:
- crates/anti-core/src/routing.rs (NEW) - CapabilityTier, ModelRoute, ProviderConfig
- .anti_subagent/providers.toml (NEW) - default config

Why config-based:
- Model landscape changes fast (GPT-5, Claude 4, etc.)
- Different teams use different providers
- No code changes needed when adding new models
- Core stays provider-agnostic

Tests:
- Scout -> Lightweight -> config-resolved model
- Engineer + High -> Heavyweight -> config-resolved model
- Missing config -> fallback to defaults
- Invalid config -> clear error message

title: 3.2: Parallel scheduler
description:
PARALLEL SCHEDULER (P3): Resource-aware, dependency-aware task scheduling for multiple peers.

ARCHITECTURE:
- Scheduler struct with max_concurrent_peers, DagGraph, ResourceMonitor
- DagGraph: task dependencies as directed acyclic graph
- ResourceMonitor: CPU/RAM usage per peer

SCHEDULING ALGORITHM:
1. Build dependency graph from task dependencies
2. Find independent sets (tasks with no unmet dependencies)
3. Check resource availability (CPU cores, RAM, model API limits)
4. Assign peers with workload balancing (round-robin or least-loaded)
5. Return Schedule with parallel groups

Schedule struct:
- parallel_groups: Vec<Vec<Task>> (tasks that can run simultaneously)
- assignments: HashMap<TaskId, PeerId> (which peer handles which task)
- resource_usage: ResourceSnapshot (current system load)

FILES:
- crates/anti-daemon/src/scheduler.rs (NEW) - Scheduler, DagGraph, ResourceMonitor
- crates/anti-daemon/src/main.rs - integrate scheduler into task dispatch

EDGE CASES:
- Circular dependencies -> detect and error
- All tasks blocked -> wait for unblocking event
- Resource exhaustion -> queue pending tasks
- Peer crash during scheduling -> reassign affected tasks

Tests:
- 3 independent tasks -> all in same parallel group
- A depends on B -> A in group after B
- max_concurrent=2, 3 tasks -> 2 parallel, 1 queued
- Resource limit reached -> queue until free

title: Phase 4: Reliability
description: P4 — 2 weeks. Restart recovery (SQLite → PID liveness → cleanup → notify), Lead handoff (context degradation → experience transfer → new Lead), Supervisor on-demand. Depends on Phase 3 scheduling.

title: 4.1: Restart recovery
description:
RESTART RECOVERY (P4): Daemon restart should recover from previous state and cleanup orphaned resources.

EXISTING CODE:
- main.rs:423 reconcile_on_start() - checks PID liveness on restart
- main.rs:468 reap_children() - marks exit status

TARGET: Enhanced restart recovery:
1. Find all RUNNING/STARTING agents in SQLite
2. Check PID liveness via kill -0 (Unix) / OpenProcess (Windows)
3. Dead process -> mark CRASHED
4. If agent had workspace lease -> Treehouse.return_if_lease()
5. Persist crash evidence (exit_code, signal, timestamp)
6. Emit PeerCrashed event
7. Lead decides: retry / replace / abort

FILES:
- crates/anti-daemon/src/main.rs - enhance reconcile_on_start()
- crates/anti-daemon/src/store.rs - add find_by_status() query

EDGE CASES:
- Agent was STARTING (not yet RUNNING) -> mark as Failed, no cleanup needed
- Workspace already cleaned by sweeper -> idempotent
- Multiple agents crash simultaneously -> process each independently
- Daemon killed mid-recovery -> SQLite state is source of truth

Tests:
- restart with live peer -> no action taken
- restart with dead peer -> cleanup + PeerCrashed event
- restart with missing workspace -> skip cleanup, log warning
- restart with multiple dead peers -> all cleaned up

title: 4.2: Lead handoff
description:
LEAD HANDOFF (P4): Context degradation after 5-7 compactions requires transferring leadership to a new Lead with preserved lessons.

TRIGGERS:
- Context degradation (compaction count > threshold)
- Manual handoff command
- Supervisor decision (on-demand governance)

HandoffContext struct:
- active_tasks: Vec<Task> (what's in progress)
- pending_reviews: Vec<Review> (awaiting decisions)
- decisions: Vec<Decision> (rationale for choices made)
- open_questions: Vec<Question> (unresolved issues)

Lesson transfer:
- Capture decisions with rationale (not just what, but why)
- Capture anti-patterns encountered
- Capture what worked well
- Format as structured JSON for new Lead consumption

FILES:
- crates/anti-daemon/src/handoff.rs (NEW) - LeadHandoff, HandoffContext, Lesson
- crates/anti-daemon/src/main.rs - integrate handoff trigger

INTEGRATION:
- New Lead spawned with HandoffContext in prompt
- Old Lead archived (not killed)
- Lessons persisted to SQLite for future reference

EDGE CASES:
- Handoff during active execution -> pause tasks, handoff, resume
- New Lead rejects handoff -> retry with different Lead
- All Leads degraded -> Supervisor intervention

Tests:
- handoff preserves all active tasks
- handoff preserves decisions with rationale
- new Lead can resume from HandoffContext
- handoff after max compactions -> automatic trigger
